records.old: 'A 2 kg Unga Pembe packet has a base area 4 times that of the 1 kg packet. What is the L.S.F between the two packets?'
records.new: 'A shop poster is an enlargement of the front face of a 1 kg Unga Pembe packet. The poster has an area 4 times the area of the packet front. What is the L.S.F between the poster and the packet?'
records.why: If a 2 kg flour packet were similar to the 1 kg packet and base area were 4 times larger, L.S.F would be 2 and the volume 2^3 = 8 times, so it would hold 8 kg, not 2 kg. For similar boxes holding 1 kg and 2 kg of flour the volume ratio is 2, so L.S.F = cube root of 2 = about 1.26 and the base area ratio is about 1.59 (1.26^2 = 1.587). That is a Lesson 6 idea, so the Lesson 5 area problem now uses a poster of the packet front, where only lengths and areas matter (L.S.F = square root of 4 = 2). The Unga Pembe supporting phenomenon in the unit (volume of boxes) is kept for Lesson 6 and later.
records.reference: KICD Grade 10 curriculum design, Mathematics, Strand 2.0, Sub-Strand 2.1 (relationship of L.S.F, A.S.F and V.S.F for similar figures and solids); standard similarity result: lengths x k, areas x k^2, volumes x k^3

records.old: It has three interlocking components: (1) a 20-minute Group Project Presentation and Mini-Exhibition in which each group displays their similar-solid models, states the L.S.F, and publicly demonstrates the squared and cubed relationships; (2) a 25-minute Driving Question Board (DQB) Review and Final Explanation in which the class collectively revisits the anchoring phenomenon — the Kisumu school plan (Scale 1 : 200) and the two water tanks — and articulates the complete answer to the driving question; and (3) a 25-minute Individual Cumulative Model-Building activity in which every learner draws and annotates a single object-to-image diagram labelling L.S.F, A.S.F, and V.S.F, writes a paragraph answering the driving question in their own words, and reflects on how their initial prediction (Lesson 1) compares with their final understanding. A 10-minute lesson close reviews outstanding DQB questions and previews Sub-Strand 2.2 (Reflection and Congruence).
records.new: It has five phases in 80 minutes: Predict (5 minutes) comparing the Lesson 1 prediction with what learners now know; Observe (20 minutes) with 2-minute group presentations of the similar-solid models, then a 5-minute gallery walk; Explain (15 minutes) revisiting the anchoring phenomenon (the Kisumu school plan at Scale 1 : 200 and the two water tanks) through the Driving Question Board (DQB) and three final-explanation prompts; Driving Question Board (12 minutes) writing and pinning Final Answer Cards; and Model Building (20 minutes) in which every learner draws and annotates a single object-to-image diagram labelling L.S.F, A.S.F, and V.S.F, writes a paragraph answering the driving question, and compares their Lesson 1 prediction with their final understanding. The remaining 8 minutes are for moving between phases and a short preview of Sub-Strand 2.2 (Reflection and Congruence).
records.why: The old overview gave 20 + 25 + 25 + 10 = 80 minutes, but the phase scripts add up to more: Predict about 6, Observe 6 groups x (3 minute presentation + about 1 minute peer comment) = 24 plus 5 gallery walk plus reading notes = about 32, Explain about 15, Driving Question Board about 13 (a group of three per card means up to 13 cards at 30 seconds each), Model Building 20 = about 86 minutes. New budget: 5 + 20 + 15 + 12 + 20 = 72 minutes plus 8 minutes of transitions and preview = 80. Teacher decides if their class size needs a different split.
records.group_headline: Lesson 8 had about 85 minutes of activity and an overview that did not match its five phases; presentations cut to 2 minutes each and a phase-by-phase time budget added

records.old: who doubles the radius of a charcoal jiko increases its cooking surface area by 4 times and its volume by 8 times
records.new: who doubles every dimension (radius and height) of a charcoal jiko increases its surface area by 4 times and its volume by 8 times
records.why: Doubling only the radius does not give 8 times the volume (a cylinder of radius r and height h has volume pi r^2 h, so doubling r alone gives 4 times). Both the 4 and the 8 hold only if every length doubles (L.S.F = 2, so 2^2 = 4 and 2^3 = 8).
records.reference: KICD Grade 10 curriculum design, Mathematics, 2.1 (A.S.F = L.S.F^2, V.S.F = L.S.F^3)

records.old: Kenyan land surveyors at the National Land Commission use exactly this logic — every boundary beacon has a grid reference, and scaling a plot on a GPS map is mathematically identical to what you just did.
records.new: Land surveyors in Kenya (for example licensed surveyors working with Survey of Kenya maps) give every boundary beacon a grid reference, and scaling a plot on a map uses the same coordinate idea you just practised: multiply the distances from a chosen point by a scale factor.
records.why: Mapping and survey standards in Kenya belong to the Survey of Kenya, not the National Land Commission (which manages public land). GPS positions are latitude and longitude, so saying enlargement is 'mathematically identical' to GPS scaling overstates it; grid references and map scaling do use the same coordinate idea.
records.group_headline: Surveying claim was inaccurate (National Land Commission, 'mathematically identical' to GPS scaling); now describes Survey of Kenya style grid references and the shared coordinate idea

records.new: Record everything on your chart.' Expected results: the A4 and A5 exercise books give length and width ratios of about 1.4 (A-series paper is similar). records.old: Distribute plain paper, rulers, sharp pencils, and geometrical sets.
records.new: Distribute plain paper, rulers, sharp pencils, and geometrical sets. Accommodation: for learners with low vision or limited hand control, give a large-print figure, let a partner hold the ruler while the learner directs where A' goes, or build the rays with string and pins (or tape) on a cardboard sheet. Learners may show the construction orally or with a photo of the string model.
records.why: No accommodations for learners with special needs were given for a construction-heavy lesson, and there was only one way to show understanding.

records.old: Observable indicator: Every learner has three written numerical predictions in their book.
records.new: Expected predictions: (a) 4 cm x 200 = 800 cm = 8 m; (b) 25 x 15 = 375 cm2, x 200^2 = 15 000 000 cm2 = 1 500 m2 (50 m x 30 m); (c) 2^3 = 8 times (many will say 2 or 4). Observable indicator: Every learner has three written numerical predictions in their book.
records.why: Expected answers were missing. Checked: 800 cm = 8 m; 25 x 200 = 5 000 cm = 50 m and 15 x 200 = 3 000 cm = 30 m, so 50 x 30 = 1 500 m2; 375 x 40 000 = 15 000 000 cm2 = 1 500 m2 (1 m2 = 10 000 cm2); tank volume factor 2^3 = 8.
records.group_headline: Added answer keys for the Lesson 7 problem cards and prediction prompts (values recomputed), so a teacher can mark them without the card sheets

records.old: Observable indicator: On Card B,
records.new: Answer guide: Card A: 1 cm on a 1 : 50 000 map is 500 m, so 1 cm2 is 0.25 km2. Card B with a 3 cm x 3 cm x 2 cm tank: real size 6 m x 6 m x 4 m, volume 144 m3 = 144 000 litres = 7 200 twenty-litre jerricans. Card C: new surface area = 1.5^2 = 2.25 times the original, new volume = 1.5^3 = 3.375 times. Observable indicator: On Card B,

records.old: Observable indicator: At least 80% of groups
records.new: Q2 answers: curved surface area 94 x 30^2 = 84 600 cm2 = 8.46 m2; grain volume 0.15 L x 30^3 = 0.15 x 27 000 = 4 050 L = 4.05 m3. Observable indicator: At least 80% of groups
records.why: The script gave the area answer but not the volume answer. Checked: 0.15 L = 150 cm3; 150 x 27 000 = 4 050 000 cm3 = 4.05 m3 (1 m3 = 1 000 000 cm3), and 4.05 m3 = 4 050 L.

records.old: All groups record working and answers on a shared group answer sheet.
records.new: All groups record working and answers on a shared group answer sheet. Where a phone, tablet or computer is available, groups that finish early check the scale of one real map online (for example comparing the printed map's scale bar with the distance tool of a web map for the same road).
records.why: The KICD suggested learning experience 'use digital devices and other resources to learn more on the use and application of similarity and enlargement' was listed in the unit's science-practice field but not carried out in any lesson. Optional, so it still works in schools without devices.
records.reference: KICD Grade 10 curriculum design, Mathematics, Strand 2.0, Sub-Strand 2.1 (suggested learning experiences)

records.old: the learner makes models of solids of different sizes (cubes, cuboids, cylinders, spheres) using locally available materials, applying similarity and enlargement concepts to design and construct them accurately.
records.new: the learner makes models of solids of different sizes using similarity and enlargement concepts. In this unit: the model-building project planned in Lesson 7 and presented in Lesson 8 (cubes, cuboids, cylinders or spheres from locally available materials).
records.why: Restores the KICD sentence for Creativity and Imagination word for word, then keeps the unit's link to the project lessons. The other KICD wording (outcomes a to f, key inquiry question, Communication and Collaboration, both values, both PCIs) already matches, with extra detail added after the KICD sentence.
records.reference: KICD Grade 10 curriculum design, Mathematics, Strand 2.0, Sub-Strand 2.1

records.old: Use the evidence you collected in Lessons 1 to 8, including your measurements, tables and models.
records.new: Use the evidence you collected in Lessons 1 to 8, including your measurements, tables, models and the Summary Table you completed. If your teacher agrees, you may give part of an answer aloud or as a labelled diagram.
records.why: The Final Explanation should say it is built from the Summary Table (guideline 7), and learners should have another way besides writing to show understanding (guideline 12).

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: States both conditions for similar figures and correctly calculates the plan width and L.S.F of 1/200, explaining clearly why proportions are preserved.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: States both conditions and calculates the L.S.F correctly, with a partly complete explanation of proportion.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: States only one condition or makes errors in converting units or finding the L.S.F.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Explains how to find the centre using ray lines, describes positive and negative k accurately, and calculates image coordinates correctly.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Describes the centre and the effect of k with minor gaps, and gets most coordinates correct.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Cannot describe how to find the centre or confuses positive and negative k.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Correctly applies A.S.F = (L.S.F)² and V.S.F = (L.S.F)³ in all calculations and explains why each rule works.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Applies both rules correctly in most calculations with a limited explanation.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Treats area or volume as scaling by k, or makes frequent calculation errors.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Connects the school plan and water tanks to the scale factor rules with clear, complete reasoning and accurate use of terms.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Connects the phenomenon to the rules with generally accurate terms but some reasoning left implicit.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Gives statements with little reasoning or little link to the phenomenon.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Gives a new, realistic Kenyan example with a correct calculation and a clear 'used to think / now I know' reflection.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Gives a suitable example with a mostly correct calculation and a brief reflection.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Example is unsuitable or the calculation is incorrect, and the reflection is missing or vague.

records.why: The contract allows only three level fields, so the CBE level names Exceeds, Meets and Approaches Expectations are now written at the start of each descriptor. Descriptor wording is otherwise unchanged.

records.why: The CBE rubric has four levels (Exceeds, Meets, Approaches, Below Expectations) but the current contract and template allow only three level fields, so the Below Expectations level cannot be represented. Suggestion: the teacher can treat any work that does not reach Approaches Expectations as Below Expectations when marking, until the contract is extended.

KICD gives Sub-Strand 2.1 Similarity and Enlargement 12 lessons; this sequence has 8 lessons (600 minutes in total) and the number of lessons cannot be changed here. All six KICD outcomes (a to f) are taught and assessed, but with 8 lessons practice time is limited (for example only one lesson each for area and volume). Teachers may wish to plan 4 extra practice lessons, for example after Lessons 4, 5, 6 and 7. Also, the unit's 'content' field restates the KICD suggested learning experiences in the data's own words; the strand and sub-strand names and numbers (Strand 2.0, 2.1) match KICD.
